8.6 — Boss Studio + Final Review

Your boss works (8.5), and the semester's final is "just a normal B day" — a normal B day where you ship the fight you have been building toward since September. Today: final polish in the morning, and the review that makes you ready to talk about everything you own.

Studio Brief ~30 min

Polish, from the spec. Open your 8.1 BOSS_SPEC.md and grade yourself line by line. Every attack has a telegraph? Phase changes are visible within one second? The arena has exactly the hazards you promised? Then the three universal upgrades:

  • Sound: a hit sound on player swing connect, a wind-up sound on charge, a death sound. Audio is half of "feel" and zero of "mechanics"
  • Hit feedback: boss flash (8.3 tinker), camera shake on charge
  • The clear screen: when the boss dies, a UI text "CAVE CLEAR" (a trigger + your HUD family) — games end with a statement, not silence

Ship freeze rules for the review: no new attacks, no new systems, no "just one more mechanic." New things break old things; the final build must be your most boring build.

Bug Hunt: The final sweep

  1. Full playthrough, spawn to boss door: entrance → all six cave beats (7.5) → the fight → the clear screen. Write every bug on paper as you go; fix them ONLY after the run.
  2. Coin economy check: how many coins can a full run collect, and what did 2.1's death loop pay on a wipe? Does death still feel cheap enough to keep trying?
Final Review ~20 min

The final is a normal B day: your game, open, playable, and a conversation about it. Practice that conversation — answer each in 30 seconds OUT LOUD:

  1. Trace a click on a coin to the counter on screen — name every method it passes through (2.1)
  2. Draw your boss's state machine from memory (4.5 + 8.2)
  3. Explain deltaTime to someone who has never coded (1.5)
  4. Why is your jump "tight"? Say the three tunables (6.3)
  5. Where did YOU use the cooldown pattern — count every instance in your game (turret, enemy damage, your swing, and…?)
  6. What does the UnityEvent on your boss's death decouple (5.2, 8.5)
  7. Which beat of your cave killed the most playtesters — and what is the data (7.7)

Socratic

One more for the road: your whole game is a program built by forking a starter. What did you INHERIT (unchanged), what did you EXTEND (changed via knobs), and what did you CREATE (new code)? Where is the line between "using a library" and "authorship"? That question is Unit 10's jam and Unit 11's Create PT rolled together.

Tinker: Ship it

  1. Build (File → Build Settings → your platform) or just pin the scene open on the lab machine — the final is the playable game, not the code
  2. Tag the release: git tag semester-1 && git push --tags
  3. Commit + push: "8.6a: semester-1 shipped"

Checkpoint — the semester, complete:

  • Spawn-to-boss full run is bug-free enough to demo to a stranger
  • Spec graded line by line; every gap has a reason, not an excuse
  • All seven review answers said out loud without notes
  • Repo tagged and pushed — the playable is the portfolio
